gaps.sentence: She earns fifty pounds ___ hour as a consultant.
gaps.explanation: 'An hour' — the 'h' is silent, so it starts with a vowel sound.

gaps.sentence: His mother went to ___ prison to visit him.
gaps.explanation: Visitors go to the building: 'went to the prison'.

gaps.sentence: He was sent to ___ prison for armed robbery.
gaps.explanation: 'Be sent to prison' (as a prisoner) takes no article; visiting the building is 'go to the prison'.

gaps.sentence: ___ sales figures for October look promising.
gaps.explanation: 'The sales figures for October' — defined by the for-phrase.

gaps.sentence: ___ Himalayas are among the youngest mountains on Earth.
gaps.explanation: Ranges like 'the Himalayas' take 'the'; single peaks take no article.

gaps.sentence: He was wearing ___ strange metal bracelet on his left wrist.
gaps.explanation: 'A strange bracelet' (first mention); body parts after prepositions traditionally take 'the' (on the left wrist).

gaps.sentence: She's got ___ few friends in Madrid, so she visits often.
gaps.explanation: 'A few' means some (positive); 'few' alone means hardly any.
'The capital of Italy' — the of-phrase makes it unique and definite.
